- [FACT] Roman roads were known for their straight construction, strong bases, and curved surfaces for water flow.
- [FACT] The Romans used a special type of concrete made from volcanic ash and lime for road construction.
- [FACT] Roman roads facilitated trade, commerce, and the movement of armies across the empire.
- [FACT] Some Roman road systems are still intact today, although they may have undergone changes in larger cities due to development.

- [QUOTE] Cristian Dima explained, "The fortitude and longevity of Roman infrastructure like roads and buildings can be attributed to their continual reuse and maintenance, along with the advanced Roman technology used during their construction."
- [FACT] Roman roads were designed to be straight and level for efficient travel and transport.
- [FACT] Roman roads had a crown, or slight upward slope towards the center, to help drain rainwater and prevent erosion.
